info.title: DEMS Core API
info.summary: Core API v1 of the DEMS Edge Client demo, as the Core server answers it: 75 operations and one WebSocket channel.
info.description:
Reference for the Core API v1 of the **DEMS Edge Client demo** (device DEMS-IR-01), as the **Core server** answers it. The design book (§21.2) names nine endpoints; this document adds their bodies, and the operations both clients need beyond them: sign-in, user administration, pairing, the session lifecycle, evidence, devices, storage, network and time, security and audit, system, alerts and the demo controls.

### Who answers

| Service | Address | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| The Core server (`dems-core-server`) | `http://127.0.0.1:4420` | Every operation of this document and `WS /ws`. It keeps the Core state in PostgreSQL and is the only authority on who may do what. Loopback only. |
| mock-core (`dems-mock-core`) | `http://127.0.0.1:4400` | `GET /api/v1/health` and a heartbeat-only `WS /ws`. It is the service of Simulated mode and answers no other operation. |
| The in-app simulator | none | In Simulated mode, the nine design-book operations (`x-dems-mode: simulated`), inside the app and without a request. Its answers carry `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header. |

Every operation carries the badge **LIVE**: the Core server answers it over the network. `x-dems-services` names the services that answer an operation, and `x-dems-mode` says whether the in-app simulator can answer it too (`simulated`) or only a service can (`live`).

### Access

The Core server decides on every request, before the body is read, from the credential the request carries:
- a **web console** sends the session cookie that `signIn` set (scheme `sessionCookie`);
- a **paired device** sends `Authorization: Bearer` (scheme `bearerAuth`): its device credential on the device operations and at sign-in, its session token once an operator is signed in.

A request carries one credential, never both. Each operation states its access rule as `x-dems-access` (PUBLIC, DEVICE, AUTHENTICATED, one permission, or the one any-of) and the audit row it writes as `x-dems-audit`. A refusal for a missing permission answers `403` and writes one audit row; the role and its permissions are read from the database for each request.

### Answers every operation shares

The answers that do not depend on the operation are defined once, under Responses: a malformed path, an unknown route, a wrong method, a server that is not ready, an Origin outside the allowed lists, two credentials in one request, the request throttle, a body over 65,536 bytes, and an unexpected failure. Every answer carries `x-request-id`, and an error repeats it as `error.requestId`. A 2xx answer of a POST carries `x-dems-epoch` and `x-dems-revision`: the state revision that holds the effect of the command.

### Lists

A list is cursor-paged: `cursor` is the `nextCursor` of the page before, `limit` is 1 to 200 (50 when omitted), and `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

### Not part of this API

- Media and evidence package files are not served: the clients keep their bundled demo media, and the server owns the records, the hashes and the verdicts.
- No operation creates or deletes a user, changes a password or edits the role matrix.
- No operation takes a file or resolves a path that a client sent.

### Examples

Examples are frozen at 2026-10-01 10:00:00 WIB and follow the canonical demo dataset: session SES-20261001-0024 (case LP/2026/1001-0007) and evidence EV-20260930-0004, exported by the SUPERVISOR operator. The nine design-book operations write times as ISO-8601 text; every other operation writes epoch milliseconds on the server clock. A password, a pairing code, a session token, a device credential and a biometric token appear only as placeholders that open nothing. All data is synthetic.

tags.description: Liveness of the service that answers: the Core server, or mock-core in Simulated mode. Public; it returns nothing of the Core state.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Sign-in, the caller's own auth session, and biometric sign-in on a paired device. The server is the only authority: a web console holds its session in an `HttpOnly` cookie, a paired device sends a bearer value. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: The role and permission matrix (read-only) and user administration: assign a role, enable, disable. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Pairing
tags.description: One-time pairing codes and the registry of paired devices. A device pairs by entering a code that a Supervisor issued. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Session lifecycle (book §6.2): CREATE → PRECHECK → ARMED → RECORDING → STOPPING → FINALIZING → SEALED, with FAULT and RECOVERY after a critical fault. One session is open per Core. The commands need SESSION_START; markers, notes and snapshots need SESSION_NOTE; every role reads the open session and the history. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the four design-book operations.

tags.name: Device
tags.description: The devices of the Core (book §6.1, §21.2): health, audio channels, video tracks, the inventory and the device commands. AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02 are reported separately in every answer. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the three design-book reads.

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Evidence storage: capacity, state, history and the retention policy. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the design-book status read.

tags.name: Evidence
tags.description: Evidence items with their tracks, hashes, custody chain and verification, and the authorized export with chain of custody (book §19.2, §19.3). No operation changes a sealed item, and none serves a media file. Answered by the Core server; in Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the design-book export.

tags.name: Network
tags.description: The network of the Core device and its time service: simulated hardware signals, read-only. The time service is not the server clock, which stamps every record. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Security
tags.description: The security status, the audit log and its hash chain, the audit and log exports, and the operational events. Every signed-in role reads; the two exports need AUDIT_EXPORT. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: System
tags.description: The Core device, its services, diagnostics, the simulated software update and the display preferences. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: The alerts of the Core and their acknowledgement. Every alert was raised by a fault, and raising it wrote a FAULT_RAISED audit row. Answered by the Core server.

tags.name: Demo
tags.description: Scenarios, fault injection and the reset to the seed state, behind DEMO_CONTROL and the server-side demo flag. Answered by the Core server.

tags.description:
WebSocket `/ws`. OpenAPI 3.1 cannot describe a socket, so it is documented here. Two services serve it:

| Service | URL | Sends |
|---|---|---|
| The Core server (`dems-core-server`) | `ws://127.0.0.1:4420/ws` | The protocol of the section "Core server": `hello`, the heartbeat, the replicated Core state, the audio meters and the control messages |
| mock-core (`dems-mock-core`) | `ws://127.0.0.1:4400/ws` | The heartbeat only (section "mock-core"): the socket of Simulated mode |

### Core server

The Core server serves `ws://127.0.0.1:4420/ws` with the protocol below. A lane instance serves the same path on its own port.

**Who a connection is.** Decided once, at the upgrade, from the request headers only: the session cookie of a web console, or `Authorization: Bearer` of a paired device. Nothing in the URL, in a subprotocol or in a message authenticates. The principal stays for the life of the connection, so a client opens a new socket after a sign-in or a sign-out.

| Principal | Receives |
|---|---|
| ANONYMOUS | `hello`, `heartbeat` |
| DEVICE | `hello`, `heartbeat`, `device.revoked` |
| OPERATOR | `hello`, `heartbeat`, `snapshot`, `delta`, `meters`, `session.updated`, `session.ended`, `device.revoked`, `admin.changed` |

**Server to client.** One JSON object per text frame; every message carries `type` and `v: 1`.

| `type` | Topic | Members | Model | Sent to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hello` | none | `connectionId`, `epoch`, `principal`, `reason?`, `topics`, `serverTime`, `heartbeatIntervalMs` | RealtimeHello | Every connection, first. |
| `heartbeat` | heartbeat | `seq`, `serverTime`, `uptimeMs`, `intervalMs`, `clients`, `sessionState` | Heartbeat | Every connection, once a second. `sessionState` is null unless the principal is OPERATOR. |
| `snapshot` | state | `epoch`, `revision`, `serverTime`, `state` | RealtimeSnapshot | OPERATOR: after `hello`, as the answer to `resync`, and when a new epoch starts. |
| `delta` | state | `epoch`, `revision`, `serverTime`, `ops` | RealtimeDelta | OPERATOR, for every change of a replicated slice. |
| `meters` | meters | `at`, `seq`, `audio` | RealtimeMeters | OPERATOR, after `subscribe`. |
| `session.updated` | control | `operator` (`id`, `role`), `permissions`, `reason` | RealtimeSessionUpdated | The sockets of the operator's sessions. |
| `session.ended` | control | `reason` | RealtimeSessionEnded | The sockets of the session, which are then closed with 4401. |
| `device.revoked` | control | `reason` | RealtimeDeviceRevoked | The sockets of the device, signed in or not, which are then closed with 4403. |
| `admin.changed` | admin | `resource` | RealtimeAdminChanged | OPERATOR holding USER_ADMIN (`USERS`) or PAIRING_MANAGE (`DEVICES`, `PAIRING_CODE`). |

**Client to server.** Anything else, or a message from a principal that may not send it, closes the connection with 1008.

| `type` | Members | Allowed for | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subscribe` | `topic: meters` | OPERATOR | The server starts the `meters` frames. |
| `unsubscribe` | `topic: meters` | OPERATOR | The server stops them. |
| `resync` | none | OPERATOR | The server answers with a new `snapshot`. At most one in 2 s; one that comes sooner is answered when the 2 s have passed. |

**State.** After `hello` an OPERATOR connection gets one `snapshot` with the 28 replicated slices (the ReplicatedState model). Every later change is a `delta` whose `revision` is the previous one plus 1 within the `epoch`: revisions have no gap, and a state delta is never dropped. A delta holds operations: `replace` carries one whole slice, `append` carries new rows of `audit` (with `head`, `total` and `dropped`) or of `events`. A slice that no operation names did not change. A client that sees a gap, or another epoch, sends `resync` (at most one in 2 s) and gets a new `snapshot`. A demo reset, a scenario load and a server start begin a new epoch. A 2xx answer of a POST carries the same two numbers in `x-dems-epoch` and `x-dems-revision`, so a client knows which delta holds the effect of its command. Not replicated: `clock`, `auth`, `authLockout`, `pairing`, `audio`. The audio frames travel in `meters` only; a client builds the other four itself, from the server time and from the answers of the identity and pairing operations.

**Time.** `heartbeat.serverTime` is an ISO-8601 string, as mock-core writes it too. Every other time of the protocol is epoch milliseconds on the server clock.

**Close codes.**

| Code | When | What a client does |
|--:|---|---|
| 1001 | Server shutdown. | Reconnect with the backoff. |
| 1008 | Protocol violation: an unknown message, one the principal may not send, or too many. | Reconnect. |
| 1009 | A client message larger than 65,536 bytes; the socket library refuses it before it is buffered. | Reconnect. |
| 1013 | The connection cap is reached. | Reconnect later. |
| 4401 | The session ended (any reason of `session.ended`), or the bearer value is not valid. | Show the login screen. A web console opens an anonymous socket for the heartbeat. |
| 4403 | The device was revoked or unpaired. | Delete the device credential and show the pairing screen. |
| 4408 | The client did not read fast enough; no state delta is dropped instead. | Reconnect and resynchronise. |

**Never in a message.** A password, a session token, a cookie value, a device credential, a biometric token, a pairing code or a QR payload, or any hash or salt of those; the `enabled` flag or the session list of another operator; the list of paired devices; the lockout state of another console. `admin.changed` names the list that changed and holds no row of it.

**Examples.**

`hello` to a signed-in investigator:

```json
{
  "type": "hello",
  "v": 1,
  "connectionId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1",
  "epoch": 3,
  "principal": "OPERATOR",
  "topics": [
    "heartbeat",
    "control",
    "state",
    "meters"
  ],
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "heartbeatIntervalMs": 1000
}
```

`hello` to a connection whose cookie no longer resolves to a session:

```json
{
  "type": "hello",
  "v": 1,
  "connectionId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a5",
  "epoch": 3,
  "principal": "ANONYMOUS",
  "reason": "SESSION_INVALID",
  "topics": [
    "heartbeat"
  ],
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "heartbeatIntervalMs": 1000
}
```

`delta`:

```json
{
  "type": "delta",
  "v": 1,
  "epoch": 3,
  "revision": 129,
  "serverTime": 1790823600000,
  "ops": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "slice": "tabletLink",
      "value": {
        "state": "CONNECTED",
        "changedAt": 1790823600000
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "append",
      "slice": "events",
      "rows": [
        {
          "id": "LOG-000061",
          "seq": 61,
          "at": 1790823600000,
          "type": "TABLET_CONNECTED",
          "severity": "INFO",
          "message": "Tablet connected",
          "params": {
            "state": "CONNECTED"
          },
          "sessionId": "SES-20261001-0024",
          "deviceId": "TABLET"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`meters`:

```json
{
  "type": "meters",
  "v": 1,
  "at": 1790823600000,
  "seq": 22440,
  "audio": {
    "channels": {
      "AUDIO-01": {
        "seq": 22440,
        "at": 1790823600000,
        "dbfs": -18.4,
        "peak": -12.1,
        "clip": false,
        "noSignal": false
      },
      "AUDIO-02": {
        "seq": 22440,
        "at": 1790823600000,
        "dbfs": -51.7,
        "peak": -50.9,
        "clip": false,
        "noSignal": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`session.updated`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.updated",
  "v": 1,
  "operator": {
    "id": "OPR-001",
    "role": "TECHNICIAN"
  },
  "permissions": [
    "EVIDENCE_VIEW",
    "DEVICE_MANAGE",
    "DIAGNOSTICS_RUN",
    "MAINTENANCE"
  ],
  "reason": "ROLE_CHANGED"
}
```

`session.ended`:

```json
{
  "type": "session.ended",
  "v": 1,
  "reason": "TOKEN_REUSE"
}
```

`device.revoked`:

```json
{
  "type": "device.revoked",
  "v": 1,
  "reason": "REVOKED"
}
```

`admin.changed`:

```json
{
  "type": "admin.changed",
  "v": 1,
  "resource": "USERS"
}
```

`subscribe`, sent by a client:

```json
{
  "type": "subscribe",
  "topic": "meters"
}
```

`resync`, sent by a client:

```json
{
  "type": "resync"
}
```

### mock-core

- Server to client only: one JSON `Heartbeat` message (see the Heartbeat model) per text frame every 1000 ms, plus one immediately after connecting.
- `seq` counts ticks since the server started. `sessionState` is `null` in this demo phase.
- Upgrades from origins other than the web dev origins and the service's own origins are refused with 403.
- Clients show the link as STALE after 2500 ms without a heartbeat and reconnect after 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s (the last delay repeats), plus up to 250 ms of jitter.
- Messages sent by clients are ignored.

Example message:

```json
{
  "type": "heartbeat",
  "v": 1,
  "seq": 5400,
  "serverTime": "2026-10-01T03:00:00.000Z",
  "uptimeMs": 5400012,
  "intervalMs": 1000,
  "clients": 2,
  "sessionState": null
}
```

Liveness of the service that answers. Public: it needs no credential and returns nothing of the Core state.

- The Core server answers `service: dems-core-server` with its version and `ready`, which says whether its database and its engine are ready. The status is `200` for as long as the process answers, so a stopped database shows as `ready.database: false`.
- mock-core, the heartbeat-only service of Simulated mode, answers `service: dems-mock-core` and no `ready`.

This is not the device health snapshot; that is `GET /api/v1/device/health`.

post.description:
Creates a session and returns its Session ID; the session enters **CREATE** (book §6.2, §12.2 steps 1-2).

Idempotent (S26): the same input while that session is still open returns it with `200` and `created: false`.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; writes the SESSION_CREATED audit row.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Runs the Core pre-check (book §5.3: 8 checks) and starts recording.

- From **CREATE**: begins the pre-check and answers `202` with state **PRECHECK**. Poll `GET /api/v1/session/current` and call again once it is **ARMED**.
- From **ARMED**: starts recording and answers `200` with state **RECORDING**.
- Pre-check ended with **WARN**: send `{"acknowledgeWarnings": true}` to acknowledge and start; without it the answer is `409 PRECHECK_WARNINGS`.
- Pre-check with a **BLOCK** (Core offline, lens fault, storage full, security fault): `409 PRECHECK_BLOCKED` with the reasons.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; the audit rows name that operator.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

A body that does not match its schema answers `422 INVALID_INPUT`. The pre-check and its outcome also have operations of their own: `beginPrecheck`, `retryPrecheck` and `acknowledgePrecheckWarnings`.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Stops the recording with a mandatory reason and moves the session to finalization: **STOPPING** → **FINALIZING** (hashes, manifest, encryption, signature) → **SEALED** (book §6.2, §12.2 steps 5-10).

Answers `202` at STOPPING; poll `GET /api/v1/session/current` for the seal.

Requires a signed-in operator holding SESSION_START; the RECORDING_STOPPED row names that operator.

One session is open per Core, and any operator holding SESSION_START may act on it. A caller whose role lacks the permission is refused with `403 NOT_PERMITTED` and one ACCESS_DENIED audit row, before the body is read.

The operator who stops a recording need not be the one who started it. A reason that is absent, or shorter than 5 characters after trimming, answers `422 INVALID_REASON` after the `404` and the `409`; a reason that is not text, holds U+0000 or an unpaired surrogate, or is longer than its maximum, and a malformed `{id}`, answer `422 INVALID_INPUT`.

The Core server's refusal texts are fixed and quote no part of the request: a session that is not the open one answers `404 NOT_FOUND` "This session is not the open session." (`details.simCode: NOT_FOUND`), and an action that does not fit the session's state answers `409 INVALID_STATE` "The action is not allowed in the current state." with `details.simCode: ILLEGAL_STATE`, `from` and `event`. A `409 SESSION_ACTIVE` names the open session in `details.sessionId`. The examples show the texts of the in-app simulator.

Answered by the Core server. In Simulated mode the in-app simulator answers the same operation inside the app, without a request, and marks its answer with the header `x-dems-simulated: 1`; the Core server never sends that header.

post.description:
Creates an auth session from a username and a password. It is accepted from exactly two kinds of caller (ID-1):

- a **web console**: the request carries a web console `Origin` and no `Authorization` header. The session is delivered only as an `HttpOnly` cookie; the body holds no token.
- a **paired device**: the request carries the device credential as `Authorization: Bearer`. The session token is returned once in `sessionToken` and is bound to that device; no cookie is set.

Any other caller gets `403 DEVICE_NOT_PAIRED`: pairing is mandatory for everything that is not a web console.

An unknown username, a wrong password and a disabled operator give the same `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, with `details.attemptsRemaining`. Every attempt writes exactly one audit row: AUTH_SUCCESS, AUTH_FAILED or AUTH_LOCKED. A valid session presented with the request is ended (rotation, ID-6).

The body or the answer holds a secret. It is never logged, and the API Reference offers no "Try it" for this operation in Live mode.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

post.description:
Creates a session from the token that the device's biometric prompt released (§5.6). The server never accepts a claim that a biometric check passed; it accepts only the token, sent with the device credential.

The body or the answer holds a secret. It is never logged, and the API Reference offers no "Try it" for this operation in Live mode.

post.description:
Pairs the calling device. The caller has no credential yet: the code is the proof. On success the device gets its ID and its credential, once, and the registry shows it as PAIRED.

A wrong, expired, used or cancelled code answers the same `401 INVALID_CODE`; the answer never says which. Three failures within 300 s lock redeeming for 60 s (`423 LOCKED`); the fifth failure closes the code.

Every attempt writes exactly one audit row: PAIRING_SUCCESS, PAIRING_FAILED or PAIRING_LOCKED. A successful redeem yields a paired device, not a session: a sign-in still follows.

The body or the answer holds a secret. It is never logged, and the API Reference offers no "Try it" for this operation in Live mode.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

post.description:
Loads one of the four scenarios: `idle`, `recording`, `finalizing`, `fault-demo`.

The Core state is rebuilt from the seed, so the audit chain restarts; the discarded chain is kept in the chain lineage. Auth sessions, paired devices, biometric tokens, settings and pairing codes are kept: nobody is signed out and no device has to pair again. While the rebuild runs, every other request answers `503 NOT_READY`.

Writes SCENARIO_LOADED as the first row after the seed history of the new chain; it names the operator, the scenario, and the head hash and row count of the discarded chain.

When the rebuild cannot run, the answer is `503 NOT_READY` with `details.reason`: `RESET_IN_PROGRESS` when another reset of this Core's database is running (try again), or `RESET_FAILED` when this one did not happen (the state is unchanged, or the server is not ready).

Needs DEMO_CONTROL and the server-side demo flag, which is off unless the server was started with it.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

post.description:
Raises one of the twelve fault kinds, with an optional target. A critical fault during a session moves it to FAULT. Every raised fault creates an alert.

Writes FAULT_RAISED; the kind AUDIT_TAMPER writes AUDIT_CHAIN_DISCONTINUITY instead. A fault that is already active writes nothing and still answers `204`.

AUDIT_TAMPER alters only the audit view the engine holds, never the stored table. TAMPER with an evidence target sets the item's tamper flag; the sealed hashes, the manifest hash and the signature are not changed.

Needs DEMO_CONTROL and the server-side demo flag, which is off unless the server was started with it.

Core server only: the in-app simulator has no such operation, so it is not available in Simulated mode.

ops.description: Applied in order. A slice no op names is not touched.

RealtimeDelta.description: One change of the replicated state. State deltas are never dropped.

seq.description: Counts the frames the server produced; a skipped frame leaves a gap, by design. It never goes back on a connection, also across a new epoch.

RealtimeMeters.description: One audio frame of both channels. Sent only after `subscribe`; it carries no revision, and the latest value wins.

operator.description: The operator of the session: ID and new role, nothing else.

permissions.description: The permissions of the new role. A display hint: the server decides every call.

RealtimeSessionUpdated.description: The role of the session's operator changed. The session stays; nobody is signed out.

RealtimeSessionEnded.description: The session of this socket ended. The server closes the connection with 4401 right after.

RealtimeDeviceRevoked.description: The device of this socket is no longer paired. The server closes the connection with 4403 right after.

RealtimeAdminChanged.description: A list of an administration page changed. It names the list only; the client refetches it through REST.

oneOf.description: Start the `meters` frames on this connection.
Stop the `meters` frames on this connection.
Ask for a new `snapshot` after a revision gap or another epoch. At most one in 2 s; one that comes sooner is answered when the 2 s have passed.

RealtimeClientMessage.description: A message a client sends on `/ws`. Anything else closes the connection with 1008; a message larger than 65,536 bytes closes it with 1009.

label.description: Label of the marker: at most 80 UTF-16 code units after trimming. Omitted or empty: the Core names it "Marker n".

text.description: The note: 1 to 2,000 characters after trimming, and at most 2,000 UTF-16 code units. It stays in the session record; the audit row holds its ID and length only.

caseNumber.description: The next case number `LP/{YYYY}/{MMDD}-NNNN`. It is reserved: the next scan offers another.

CaseNumberScan.description: Result of the simulated case-number scanner.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

PageQuery.description: Query of a list read that takes no filter: the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Finished sessions, newest first: the elements of the `sessionHistory` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

SessionHistoryPage.description: One page of the session history.

caseType.description: Only items of this case type (the subject type of the session).

q.description: Search text, 1 to 100 characters after trimming: matched without regard to case against the evidence ID, the session ID, the case number and the subject name.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

EvidenceListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/evidence`: filters, a search text and the paging members of API-9.

items.description: Evidence items, newest recording first: the elements of the `evidence` slice.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

source.description: DEMO_PACKAGE: the demo package a client bundles belongs to this item. NONE: no media exists for it (a session recorded in Live mode).

packageSuffix.description: The join key of the bundled package, e.g. `0004`; null when the source is NONE.

EvidenceMediaRef.description: Which bundled media belongs to an evidence item. It names no file and no path: the server serves no media (MS-1, MS-3).

EvidenceDetail.description: One evidence item and the reference to its media.

ok.description: True when every track, the manifest and the signature verify.

at.description: When the verification ran, on the server clock.

expected.description: The sealed hash of the track.

tracks.description: One result per track: VIDEO-01, VIDEO-02, AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02, each on its own.

EvidenceVerifyResult.description: The verdict of record of an integrity verification: the simulator's `EvidenceVerifyResult`.

DeviceInventory.description: The devices of the Core: seven slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

cameraId.description: The camera the monitor shows: VIDEO-01 or VIDEO-02.

channel.description: The audio channel whose CLIP latch is reset: AUDIO-01 or AUDIO-02.

StorageDetail.description: The storage of the Core and its retention policy: two slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

retentionPolicy.description: The retention policy. Sent without `retentionDays`, it sets the days of that policy: 30, 90, 365 or 3,650.

retentionDays.description: Days an item is kept before it may be archived: a whole number from 1 to 3,650.

autoArchive.description: Whether an item is archived by itself when its retention ends.

StoragePolicyRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/storage/policy`: the members to change. A member that is left out keeps its value.

NetworkStatus.description: The network of the Core and the link of the tablet: two slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

TimeStatus.description: The time service of the Core device: one slice of the Core state in its wire form, under its slice name.

auditHead.description: Hash of the newest audit row of the stored chain; 64 zeros when the chain is empty.

auditTotal.description: Rows of the stored chain: the `seq` of its newest row.

SecurityStatus.description: The `security` slice in its wire form, with the head and the row count of the audit chain.

type.description: Only rows of this audit type.

actorId.description: Only rows whose actor is this operator (`OPR-NNN`).

evidenceId.description: Only rows of this evidence item.

order.description: By `seq`: ASC is the order of the chain, oldest first, and is used when omitted; DESC is newest first.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

AuditListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/audit`: filters, the order and the paging members of API-9.

rows.description: Audit rows in the order asked for, each with its full hashed body.

head.description: Hash of the newest row of the stored chain at the time of the read.

total.description: Rows of the stored chain at the time of the read, whatever the filters.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

AuditPage.description: One page of audit rows. Rows are ordered by `seq`, so paging stays stable while rows are appended.

checked.description: Rows checked: every row of the view.
Rows that verified before the first bad one.

index.description: Position of the first bad row in the view (`audit.rows`).

ChainVerifyResult.description: Result of the shared chain check over the audit view: the simulator's `ChainVerifyResult`.

epoch.description: The epoch the discarded chain ended in.

head.description: Head hash of the discarded chain.

resetAt.description: When the reset ran, on the server clock.

actorId.description: The operator who ran it; null for a reset from the command line.

scenario.description: The scenario the reset loaded (`idle` for a reset to the seed state).

AuditChainLineageEntry.description: One audit chain that a demo reset or a scenario load discarded.

view.description: The shared check over the audit view the engine holds: what the screens show, and what the demo fault AUDIT_TAMPER breaks.

checked.description: The `seq` the stored chain has been verified through.

head.description: Head hash of the stored chain.

firstBadSeq.description: `seq` of the first stored row that does not verify; null while the chain verifies.

stored.description: The check over the stored table, which no demo fault can break. It is incremental: a call verifies only the rows above the last verified one.

lineage.description: The chains that earlier resets discarded, newest first, at most 20.

lineageTotal.description: How many chains were discarded in all.

AuditChainStatus.description: Status of the audit chain: the view, the stored table, and the lineage of discarded chains.

reason.description: Purpose of the export: 5 to 500 characters after trimming. It is recorded in the AUDIT_EXPORTED row.

destination.description: Destination or approved media identifier: at most 120 UTF-16 code units after trimming. Omitted or empty means "Audit archive (simulated)".

rows.description: Stored audit rows the export covers: every row before the AUDIT_EXPORTED row it wrote.

head.description: Hash of the last of those rows: the `prevHash` of the AUDIT_EXPORTED row.

AuditExportAccepted.description: Export accepted. The ExportEvent is the AUDIT_EXPORTED audit row it wrote; the client builds the file.

cursor.description: Opaque position: the `nextCursor` of the page before. Omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Rows of the page: 1 to 200. The server uses 50 when it is omitted.

EventListQuery.description: Query of `GET /api/v1/events`: filters and the paging members of API-9.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next page, or null when this page is the last.

EventPage.description: One page of operational events. Events are ordered by `seq`, so paging stays stable while events are appended.

SystemStatus.description: The system page of the Core: five slices of the Core state, each in its wire form.

runId.description: ID of the run, `DIAG-NNNNNN`. Its checks resolve in the `diagnostics` slice.

DiagnosticsRunStarted.description: A diagnostics run was started, or one is still in progress.

restarted.description: How many Core services were restarted: every one that was not stopped.

ServicesRestarted.description: Result of a restart of the Core services.

SettingsUpdateRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/v1/settings`: the display preferences to change. A member that is left out keeps its value.

AlertList.description: The alerts of the Core: one slice of the Core state in its wire form, under its slice name.

XRequestId.description: The ID of the request in the Core server's log. An error envelope repeats it as `error.requestId`.

XDemsEpoch.description: The epoch of the Core state: it counts demo resets and scenario loads. An integer, sent as decimal text (API-7).

XDemsRevision.description: The revision of the delta that holds the command's effect (the current revision when nothing replicated changed). An integer, sent as decimal text; it restarts at 0 with each epoch (API-7).

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds until the caller's key is counted afresh.

InvalidPath.description: 400 INVALID_PATH. The path is malformed, or a path parameter is not valid percent-encoding.

NotFound.description: 404 NOT_FOUND. No operation has this path.

MethodNotAllowed.description: 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. The path exists, but not with this method.

NotReady.description: 503 NOT_READY. The database or the engine is not ready, or a demo reset is running. Every operation except health.

OriginNotAllowed.description: 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED. The `Origin` header is not on the list that fits the credential the request carries (01_specs §14.2).

CredentialConflict.description: 401 NOT_SIGNED_IN (`details.reason: CREDENTIAL_CONFLICT`). The request carries a session cookie and an `Authorization` header: one credential per request (ID-12).

RateLimited.description: 429 RATE_LIMITED. The request throttle, or the denial budget of the caller's key (20 audited refusals in 60 s), is used up.

PayloadTooLarge.description: 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. The request body is larger than 65,536 bytes.

InvalidJson.description: 400 INVALID_JSON. A body was sent that is not a JSON object. Every POST, also one that takes no body; an empty body is no body.

InternalError.description: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR or SIMULATOR_ERROR. An unexpected failure; the answer holds no detail. SIMULATOR_ERROR is the in-app simulator's code.

sessionCookie.name: dems_session_4420
sessionCookie.description: The session of a web console. `signIn` sets it as an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie without an expiry, and its body then holds no token; the browser attaches the cookie to same-origin requests and to the socket upgrade. The name is `dems_session_<listen port>`: `dems_session_4420` on the main instance. It resolves only a session that is not bound to a device, and a POST that carries it must come from a web console origin.

bearerAuth.description: A paired device. `Authorization: Bearer` carries the device credential (prefix `dvc_`) on the device operations and at sign-in, and the session token (prefix `ses_`) once an operator is signed in on the device. The server stores only a hash of either. One credential per request: a request that carries the session cookie and this header is refused. Neither value ever travels in a URL.
